transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brought me in is that things just got kind of out of hand recently. I went from just being a normal crew guy at work to... well, trying to run three different bids at once. I was calling city people, trying to line up plant suppliers, and just messaging everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. It was like I couldn’t shut it off.
Have you felt like your thoughts were racing, or that you had more energy or needed less sleep during this time?

Yeah, definitely. My head was just running so fast. I had all these plant lists, slogans, ideas for park layouts, and lists of who I needed to impress just constantly going through my mind. I would sit down and fill whole pages in a notebook with it all, and I'd still feel like I was falling behind my own thoughts. It just wouldn't stop.
After this period of high energy and racing thoughts, did you experience a time where you felt very down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I did. After all that park stuff fell apart, I just... crashed. I felt really down and just kind of empty. Usually, when I need to clear my head, I'll go hiking. I like taking pictures of creek beds and trees, looking for the right lighting and all that. But lately, I haven't even been doing that. I just leave my camera sitting in the truck. I don't really care if the light is perfect or not anymore. I just don't have any interest in it right now.
Have you ever had a period where you felt so good or so hyper that you didn't want to stop what you were doing, even if it meant taking big chances or not sleeping at all?

Yeah, that's exactly how it was. During that whole time, I'd be up way before daylight, just... loading tools into the truck, sketching out new beds, and pricing out native plants. And then I'd go work a full day outside at my regular job. But even after all that physical work, I still felt like I had to keep going. I just didn't want to stop or sleep at all.
Have you ever had a time when you felt so powerful or confident that you thought you could do things no one else could, or that others would describe as extreme or out of character for you?

Yeah, I did. I mean, during that whole park layout phase... I honestly believed I was about to become the guy every town around here called for sustainable landscaping. I was just so sure of it. Looking back, it's pretty out there, because, you know, I’m still just trying to keep my small jobs paid up. But at the time, I really felt like I was on another level and nobody could do it better than me.
